transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20
Time: 14:00 - 15:02 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Sara Kim (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (NovaSearch, Head of Search), Priya Patel (Engineering Manager), Tom Alvarez (SRE)
---
Summary: quick hosted API demo focusing on embeddings + reranking flow for search relevance, walked through Console for routing and Optimize suggestions, discussed latency/cost tradeoffs and security requirements; agreed to a short pilot + benchmarks.
---
Topics: embeddings model selection, vector store vs managed index, two-stage search (ANN -> rerank), Redwood Console quickstart, Redwood Optimize batch/caching suggestions, security (VPC, KMS, SOC2), pilot next steps
---
Transcript:
[00:00] Sara Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sara from Redwood, and with me is Diego on the engineering side. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Liam Chen: Good, thanks, Sara. Excited to see the walkthrough — we had a quick call with your solutions team last week.
[00:11] Priya Patel: Hi all, Priya here. We'll mostly be tuning search relevance for our docs + support portal, and Liam's flagged some latency concerns.
[00:18] Diego Morales: Great. Quick agenda — I'll show a short demo of the Hosted API embeddings endpoint, then the rerank endpoint and how we wire them into a two-stage retrieval pipeline. After that I'll flip over to the Console and Redwood Optimize to show cost/latency suggestions.
[00:30] Tom Alvarez: Sounds good. We also want to know about VPC/private deployment options if needed from a compliance perspective.
[00:35] Sara Kim: We'll cover that too — quick note, NovaSearch mentioned they are evaluating Elastic and Pinecone — we can address tradeoffs as we go.
[00:42] Diego Morales: Ok, jumping in. First, embeddings. Redwood Hosted API offers /v1/embeddings — you POST text and choose a model, we return a dense vector. Example payload in the demo app: {"input": "How to reset password", "model": "redwood-embed-small"} — then we get a 768-d vector back.
[01:08] Liam Chen: Quick question: do you host the vectors or do we need to push to our vector DB?
[01:12] Diego Morales: Good Q. Two modes: you can host vectors in your own store (Pinecone, Milvus, Elasticsearch) or use Redwood's managed index via the Console. For the demo I'm showing managed first — it's easier to get started. Under the hood we store ephemeral vectors and expose nearest-neighbor queries.
[01:26] Priya Patel: Are there guarantees about retention and exportability?
[01:29] Diego Morales: Yes — you can export vectors and data anytime via the Console or API. For Private deployments we also support customer-managed KMS.
[01:36] [01:36] Diego Morales (screen share): Here in the Console you can create an Index, pick an embeddings model, and set vector dimension/metric. I'm uploading a small dataset of 5k docs for this demo.
[01:50] [02:00] Diego Morales: Now once you have an ANN search you typically fetch top-K hits, say top-50, and then rerank. Redwood offers a /v1/rerank endpoint — you pass the query, the candidate documents, and a model chooser (we have both classification-style and pairwise rerankers). The endpoint returns a re-ordered list with scores.
[02:18] Liam Chen: So the idea is ANN is cheap and fast, rerank is more expensive but done only on the small candidate set?
[02:23] Diego Morales: Exactly. It reduces total cost and improves final relevance. For example we show 2-3x relevance lift on our sample evals when moving from ANN-only to ANN+rerank.
[02:34] Tom Alvarez: What about latency? Our SLA target is 150ms p95 for search queries.
[02:39] Diego Morales: In Hosted mode, typical ANN retrieval is 20-60ms depending on size; rerank depends on model — small pairwise reranker can be ~30-80ms for 50 candidates. Combined with network overhead you can hit ~100-180ms p95. If you need consistent sub-150ms p95 we recommend a smaller candidate set (top-20) or embedded quantized models, or Dedicated capacity.
[03:02] Priya Patel: And cost? We have millions of queries per month.
[03:06] Sara Kim: We price embeddings per call and rerank per token or per candidate depending on reranker type — we'll share a pricing sheet after. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching and caching rules to reduce calls to the rerank endpoint for repeated prefixes.
[03:17] [03:25] Diego Morales (demo continues): I'll run a live query — here is the query vector, we call the index to get top-50, then call /v1/rerank with pairwise model. You can see the before vs after ordering. (slight lag) The highlighted doc jumps from rank 9 to rank 1 after rerank.
[03:48] Liam Chen: Looks promising. A couple of our edge cases are short queries and misspellings; how do you handle normalization or fuzzy matches?
[03:56] Diego Morales: We recommend a hybrid approach: lexical filters for exact matches, and embeddings for semantic similarity. The reranker can incorporate lexical features (bm25 scores, token overlap) as additional inputs.
[04:10] Priya Patel: Any tooling for A/B testing different rerank models?
[04:14] Diego Morales: Yes, Console supports rollout policies — you can do canary or weighted traffic between rerank variants, and Redwood Optimize will track quality metrics against your eval prompt set.
[04:24] Liam Chen: You mentioned caching — is that query-level or prefix-level?
[04:28] Diego Morales: Both. We support prefix/KV caching for completions and also result-level caching for popular queries. Optimize will suggest TTLs based on usage patterns.
[04:36] Tom Alvarez: Security: SAML/SSO, audit logs, and data residency. What can you share?
[04:42] Sara Kim: We are SOC 2 Type II and ISO-ready; we provide audit logs, RBAC, SSO (SAML), and for Private deployments we support VPC peering and customer KMS. I'll attach the security pack after the call.
[04:55] Priya Patel: For a pilot we can't send PII externally — can we run a trial in Dedicated or Private?
[05:01] Sara Kim: Yes — Dedicated reserved pools or Private deployment are options; for the pilot we can provision a short-lived Dedicated instance or run the benchmark on Private if you prefer. Diego can help scope.
[05:12] [05:20] Diego Morales: I'll sketch a plan: we run a 2-week pilot with your sample dataset. Step 1: NovaSearch provides sample queries and success criteria. Step 2: Redwood provision trial API key + managed index, run an initial baseline with your current Elastic results. Step 3: Run ANN+rerank, get metrics on relevance (MRR/NDCG) and latency/cost.
[05:39] Liam Chen: That matches what we wanted. About failure modes — what happens when the reranker times out?
[05:44] Diego Morales: We have graceful fallback policies: if the rerank endpoint times out we can return ANN-only results; Console lets you set timeouts and fallback models. You can also configure automatic retries and rate-limit policies.
[05:57] Priya Patel: Any integration examples for our stack? We're on GCP, using BigQuery and a managed vector store.
[06:03] Diego Morales: We have SDKs in Python/Node and example connectors for Pinecone and Milvus; for GCP customers we provide a managed connector template. We'll share the repo link in the follow-up.
[06:14] [06:28] Diego Morales (typing): I'm switching to Optimize — here Optimize suggests quantized models for rerank when latency matters and recommends batch sizes for embeddings ingestion. For your workload, Optimize suggests batch size 64 for ingestion and top-K=20 for retrieval to keep p95 under 150ms while controlling cost.
[06:45] Liam Chen: How do you measure relevance regressions?
[06:48] Diego Morales: You provide eval prompt sets — Optimize runs production-like tests and emits regression alerts tied to prompt sets. We also support automated A/B comparisons and synthetic holdouts.
[06:58] Tom Alvarez: From an SRE perspective we want observability — tracing, token-level cost, per-route dashboards.
[07:04] Sara Kim: Console has per-route latency/cost breakdowns, request tracing hooks, and you can export metrics to Datadog/Prometheus. We'll include screenshots.
[07:14] [07:25] Diego Morales: Demo wrap-up — major benefits: faster iteration (hosted API + Console), measurable relevance lift with rerank, and Optimize gives concrete levers to tune cost/latency.
[07:36] Priya Patel: What about model upgrades — if you change the embeddings model, how do we detect regressions?
[07:41] Diego Morales: Optimize has model comparison workflows; you run candidate models on a holdout and compare NDCG/MRR. Also you can pin models per-route during rollouts.
[07:52] Liam Chen: Ok, next steps — we'll send a small dataset and our success criteria, and we'd like a pilot.
[07:58] Sara Kim: Great — we'll send the pricing and security docs, Diego will prepare the benchmark harness. Any other questions?
[08:05] Tom Alvarez: Thumbs up from SRE. One more: networking — can you support VPC peering for Hosted, or is that only Private?
[08:12] Sara Kim: Hosted supports private networking options for enterprise tiers (VPC peering and private endpoints) but if you need full air-gapped that's Private. We'll clarify in the security doc.
[08:21] Priya Patel: Perfect.
[08:24] Sara Kim: Okay — quick recap of action items and owners. Diego?
[08:27] Diego Morales: I'll run the benchmark and share the harness; Sara will send pricing and security docs; Liam will provide sample queries and success criteria.
[08:35] Sara Kim: Thanks everyone! We'll follow up with the trial key and timelines.
[08:40] Liam Chen: Thanks, appreciate the demo.
[08:42] End of call.
